entries.name: Reveal
entries.summary: Reveal — animate a single element into view with a named profile. <Reveal profile="slideLeft" as="p">…</Reveal> Honours reduced motion (static).
entries.description:
Reveal — animate a single element into view with a named profile.
<Reveal profile="slideLeft" as="p">…</Reveal>
Honours reduced motion (static).

IMPORTANT: this component must NOT re-render on scroll. It used to subscribe
to the fast-scroll governor and swap its `variants`/`viewport` objects on
every scroll burst — which made Framer Motion tear down and recreate the
`whileInView` observer, replaying the entrance over and over (sections
visibly "collapsing and reappearing" while scrolling). The variants and
viewport config are memoised here so their identity is stable; with
`once: true` Motion keeps the original observer, fires the entrance exactly
once, then disconnects.

`will-change` / `filter` / `clip-path` housekeeping lives in the profiles
themselves (see `withHousekeeping` in revealProfiles.js).

entries.name: SceneCanvas
entries.summary: Renders a single registered scene onto a canvas. - the scene library is loaded on demand (code-split) via ensureScenes() - each scene registers with the SCENE BUDGET: only the few most-visible scenes animate at once;
entries.description:
Renders a single registered scene onto a canvas.
- the scene library is loaded on demand (code-split) via ensureScenes()
- each scene registers with the SCENE BUDGET: only the few most-visible
scenes animate at once; the rest hold a static frame (the core anti-lag)
- the rAF draw is throttled to ~30fps (backgrounds don't need 60/120Hz)
- DPR-capped + quality-scaled by the motion budget
- a single static frame under reduced motion (or when `still`), never loops
- fully torn down (loop, budget, observers, scene.dispose) on unmount

Wraps a section with its own animated scene behind the content. This is how

intensity  'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'hero'  (default 'medium')
accent     #hex accent passed to the scene

entries.description:
---- the engine ----------------------------------------------------------------
Sim owns a canvas and a loop. `setup(S)` builds the state once (it is kept in
S.st); `tick(S, dt)` advances and draws one frame. S carries the context, the
size, the clock, the pointer (S.in, in canvas pixels) and a queue of clicks.

entries.name: Specimen
entries.summary: A specimen: one component on show. The frame (its look is the page's `frame`, set on the stage as data-frame) carries a code, the name and how to use it (click, drag, hover, type, auto…).
entries.description:
A specimen: one component on show. The frame (its look is the page's `frame`,
set on the stage as data-frame) carries a code, the name and how to use it
(click, drag, hover, type, auto…). It tells its contents whether it is on
screen, so loops can stop while it is not, and it is `inert` while a stage has
it out of reach (offscreen on a belt, behind the camera) so keyboard focus
never disappears into a clipped region.

entries.name: CanvasStage
entries.summary: CANVAS STAGES — the page is a sheet, not a column. The specimens sit on a big flat plane and the scroll flies a camera between them (camera.js): it rests on one, pulls back until the way to the next is in view, swings across — left, right,…
entries.description:
CANVAS STAGES — the page is a sheet, not a column. The specimens sit on a
big flat plane and the scroll flies a camera between them (camera.js):
it rests on one, pulls back until the way to the next is in view, swings
across — left, right, up or down — and drops back in. Three plans share the
machinery: `canvas` (a fractal wander), `atlas` (a sheet read in rows) and
`spiral` (winding outward).

Like every stage this never re-renders per frame: the hook hands over the
scroll position and camera.js turns it into where the camera is. That goes
straight into the world's own transform — not into custom properties on an
ancestor, which would make the browser re-style every element of every
specimen on every frame. The hook's own numbers (--pin and the rest) go to a
small overlay that holds the monitor, the map and the readout.

entries.name: Stage
entries.summary: Picks the engine for a page: its own, unless the screen or the visitor asks for the plain one (or the sheet was asked for).

entries.name: Hud

Browser effects clean up when the component unmounts. See the source for all optional arguments.

entries.description:
Writes the pointer's position INSIDE an element to CSS variables, so any
descendant can respond with pure CSS (transforms, gradients, parallax).

Pointer-proximity engine. Finds every `[data-prox]` unit inside `ref` and
keeps a CSS variable --k (0..1) on each: 1 under the cursor, easing to 0 at

entries.description:
Owns the ambient <audio> element and a single Web Audio graph
(MediaElementSource -> AnalyserNode -> destination). The graph is built
lazily on the first user gesture (autoplay-safe) and reused for the
session. Exposes real frequency data so the visualizer reacts to sound.
The track is `src` (or configureAssets({ musicSrc })); the library ships none.

`status` is the single source of truth for every audio control on the site
(navbar, mobile menu, boot). It follows the <audio> element's own events —
not just our calls — so the controls stay correct when the browser pauses
playback, when the file is still loading, or when a play() request is
rejected by the autoplay policy:

idle     nothing playing (default)
loading  play() was requested; waiting for the first audible frame
playing  audible
blocked  the browser refused play() (no user activation); press again
error    the track failed to load

entries.name: initPerformanceMode
entries.summary: PERFORMANCE MODE — the fast-scroll governor.
entries.description:
PERFORMANCE MODE — the fast-scroll governor.

A single global module tracks scroll velocity and broadcasts a coarse
performance mode that the whole app reads to decide how hard to work:

  'normal'      — animate normally
  'fast-scroll' — the user is flinging the page; freeze scenes, snap reveals,
                  disable pointer-reactive effects, skip eager scene painting
  'reduced'     — prefers-reduced-motion; nothing heavy ever runs

One scroll listener, one timer, ref-based — no React state in the hot path.
Scenes / reveals / cursor subscribe and react. The core anti-lag for fast
scrolling: we stop trying to animate every block the user flies past.

entries.name: subscribePerformanceMode
entries.summary: Subscribe to mode changes. Returns an unsubscribe fn.

entries.name: initViewportDirector
entries.summary: VIEWPORT DIRECTOR — stable, correct viewport sizing.
entries.description:
VIEWPORT DIRECTOR — stable, correct viewport sizing.

Browsers' `100vh` is wrong on mobile (URL bar) and `svh/dvh` aren't always
enough for our full-screen stages. This writes a measured pixel height to
CSS custom properties that stages read, and keeps scene/scroll layout in
sync after resize/orientation so animations never run on stale dimensions
(the cause of the "1.5 blocks on load" + glitch-on-resize bugs).

  --viewport-h : measured viewport height in px
  --vh         : 1% of that, for `calc()`

Updates are debounced; after settling it dispatches `hanoryx:layout-settled`
so ScrollTrigger / Lenis / scenes can refresh once, cleanly.

entries.name: copyText
entries.summary: Copy text to the clipboard. Uses the async Clipboard API where the browser allows it, and a hidden textarea where it does not (older browsers, or a page that is not a secure context). Resolves to whether it worked.

entries.name: downloadText
entries.summary: Save text as a file the visitor downloads. Nothing leaves the browser: the file is built in memory and handed to a temporary link.

entries.name: parseHex
entries.summary: '#abc', 'abc', '#aabbcc' -> [r, g, b], or null when it is not a hex colour.

entries.name: contrastRatio
entries.summary: The WCAG contrast ratio of two colours, from 1 (identical) to 21 (black on white).

entries.name: nearestPassing
entries.summary: The closest colour to `fg` (changing only its lightness) that reaches `target` against `bg`, looking both darker and lighter. Returns { darker, lighter }, either of which may be null.

entries.name: parseCron
entries.summary: Parse an expression. Returns { ok: true, text, fields, sets, star } or { ok: false, error }.

entries.name: expand
entries.summary: The values a field expands to, written for a person.

entries.name: describe
entries.summary: One sentence that says when it runs.

entries.name: warnings
entries.summary: Things worth knowing about this particular schedule.

entries.name: nextRuns
entries.summary: The next `count` run times (as epoch milliseconds) after `fromMs`, in the local zone or in UTC.

entries.name: clearOwnStorage
entries.summary: Remove only the site's own items. Returns how many were removed.

entries.name: fx
entries.summary: Marks a foreground detail so it can be inventoried and (in blueprint mode) labelled. `fx('home.orbit')` spreads `data-fx="home.orbit"` onto an element. It has no runtime cost beyond the attribute.
entries.description:
Marks a foreground detail so it can be inventoried and (in blueprint mode)
labelled. `fx('home.orbit')` spreads `data-fx="home.orbit"` onto an element.
It has no runtime cost beyond the attribute. qa/foreground-inventory.mjs
loads every route and counts the distinct markers that actually render.

entries.name: changesIn
entries.summary: Every clock change a zone makes in a year, found by watching the offset day by day. Each result: { at, before, after, y, m, d } where y/m/d is the local date of the change.

entries.name: effectOn
entries.summary: What `HH:MM` does on the local day of a clock change: 0 = it never happens, 1 = once, 2 = twice.

entries.name: loadPageCatalog
entries.summary: Lightweight title, intro and reading metadata for every page, from the registered source.

entries.name: configureSite
entries.summary: Register any of: loadPage(key), warmPage(pathname), loadPageCatalog(), loadSearchDocuments(), company, navigation.

entries.name: architectural-grid
entries.summary: Technical blueprint surface: major + minor grid, measuring ticks, corner crosshair marks and dimension dashes, with a slow vertical drift and a single red crosshair node tracing the grid like a CAD cursor.

entries.name: blackout-silhouette
entries.summary: A hidden silhouette under redaction. Faint hatched black regions conceal an abstract geometric form; a vertical scan line sweeps across and briefly reveals the red edge contours where it passes, then re-conceals.

entries.name: circuit-trace
entries.summary: PCB-like traces with pulses travelling along right-angle paths.

entries.name: command-terminal
entries.summary: A terminal readout — monospace log lines scan in sequence, a caret blinks on the active line, and a faint highlight bar sweeps down the column. One red WARN line. Static strings, low-alpha white; mysterious technical mood.

entries.name: concentric-gate
entries.summary: Concentric gate rings that draw open in staggered arcs — portal / hero core.

entries.name: data-rain
entries.summary: Restrained vertical data columns — measured, not a Matrix spam wall.

entries.name: flow-field
entries.summary: Optimized particle flow field with pointer displacement. Trails via a low alpha fill over the (near-black) section. Density scales with quality.

entries.name: glass-prism
entries.summary: Angular translucent glass panels — rotated quads with faint white gradient fills and crisp edges, drifting and parallaxing as layered glass.

entries.name: glyph-field
entries.summary: A sparse grid of abstract glyphs — small geometric marks (+, circles, brackets, short bars) that breathe in and out and occasionally swap form, like an unknown symbol language slowly writing itself.

entries.name: heatmap-grid
entries.summary: Operational heatmap: a grid of cells whose intensity pulses as a sum of slow sine waves over position + time. Bright cells take a faint red tint, dim cells stay barely-there white.

entries.name: hex-lattice
entries.summary: Hexagon lattice with a travelling scan that lights nodes as it passes.

entries.name: isometric-module
entries.summary: Isometric cubes drifting through depth — faint white volumes that bob and parallax. One cube is edge-lit in the accent red. 2:1 iso projection.

entries.name: liquid-metal
entries.summary: Soft elliptical blobs drifting and breathing — a calm metallic sheen. Large radial-gradient ellipses overlap with very low alpha; no hard edges.

entries.name: magnetic-particles
entries.summary: Particles drifting in a slow ambient field, magnetically drawn toward the pointer when active — pulled in, brightened, then easing back when released.

entries.name: network-constellation
entries.summary: Connected graph with light physics drift — a constellation / service map. Connections use a spatial cap (nearest by distance) to stay cheap.

entries.name: orbital-node
entries.summary: Concentric orbits of nodes circling a core — multi-role / system map feel.

entries.name: polar-radar
entries.summary: Rotating radar sweep with concentric rings and bearing ticks.

entries.name: architecture-layer
entries.summary: ARCHITECTURE LAYER — a system blueprint of 4-5 stacked slab layers drawn in a slight isometric skew, joined by vertical connectors; a red data pulse rises through the stack, briefly lighting each layer it passes.

entries.name: audio-signal-wall
entries.summary: AUDIO SIGNAL WALL — full-width spectrum visualizer. Reacts to live audio via the shared audio bridge; falls back to a procedural idle signal when nothing is playing. A faint baseline grid + a mirrored reflection give it depth.

entries.name: build-pipeline
entries.summary: BUILD PIPELINE — 5 stage gates chained left to right; a build token advances gate by gate, each cleared stage fills with a check-tick pulse, and an occasional parallel branch forks below. A CI/build shape language.

entries.name: client-portal-gate
entries.summary: CLIENT PORTAL GATE — two concentric iris rings of arc blades that rhythmically open (gaps widen) then re-seal like an aperture, a rotating radial scan beam sweeps the field, and a locked diamond core glyph blinks red on each seal.

entries.name: commerce-pipeline
entries.summary: COMMERCE PIPELINE — horizontal lanes carry small order tokens left to right through vertical stage gates; a soft scan band sweeps across, and the rare flagged order glows red. A logistics/order-flow shape language, no grid.

entries.name: compass-vector
entries.summary: Canvas scene "compass-vector".

entries.name: contact-transmission
entries.summary: CONTACT TRANSMISSION — concentric ping rings emit outward from a source point at timed intervals over faint carrier waves, with a few drifting signal motes.

entries.name: dashboard-tiles
entries.summary: DASHBOARD TILES — a bento grid of varied-size panels, each running a tiny live widget (sparkline, mini bars, blinking dot, gauge arc, ticker), while a single red focus highlight glides from tile to tile like a roving control cursor.

entries.name: data-interface-wave
entries.summary: Canvas scene "data-interface-wave".

entries.name: data-stream-ribbons
entries.summary: DATA STREAM RIBBONS — several bright thin straight diagonal ribbons of flowing dashes carrying data in transit; bright packet glints ride each stream over a faint baseline grid. Straight diagonal dash flow, not braided curves.

entries.name: dependency-graph
entries.summary: DEPENDENCY GRAPH — modules in left-to-right layers wired by directed edges (a build DAG); a build wave sweeps left to right, compiling each layer: edges fill and node cores ignite in order.

entries.name: error-signal-lost
entries.summary: ERROR / SIGNAL LOST (404) — a near-flat heartbeat trace that twitches, glitches and drops out into a dead flatline, intermittent horizontal static bands tear across the screen, and a faint radar sweep hunts the void but finds nothing.

entries.name: glyph-compiler
entries.summary: GLYPH COMPILER — scattered mono glyphs drift in space, then snap into neat left-aligned rows (compiling), hold as clean labels, then dissolve back to scatter. A red caret/scan rides the row that is currently resolving.

entries.name: heatmap-control
entries.summary: HEATMAP CONTROL — a dashboard heatmap: a tight grid of cells lit by several smooth gaussian "activity" blobs drifting across the field; warmth fades cell to cell, and only the hottest cells latch a sparse red accent outline.

entries.name: hex-tunnel
entries.summary: HEX TUNNEL — concentric hexagons surge outward from a vanishing point toward the viewer, each ring slightly counter-rotated and fading with depth; one pulsing red ring rides the loop. Built ring-by-ring (not a flat lattice).

entries.name: home-core
entries.summary: HOME CORE — the cinematic hero composite: a faint scrolling grid, a central arc/gate system that breathes, and a sparse particle field drifting over it. Pointer nudges the core. The most layered scene in the library.

entries.name: interface-lab-shape
entries.summary: INTERFACE LAB SHAPE — abstract UI "component" specimens (toolbars, cards, toggles) as rounded-rect outlines with corner brackets that snap to a grid and periodically resize / rearrange between layout takes.

entries.name: isometric-infra
entries.summary: ISOMETRIC INFRA — a blueprint isometric module field where lit modules sweep across in travelling diagonal clusters; a few of the brightest modules extrude tall vertical "data columns" that pulse upward. Faint base lattice, sparse red.

entries.name: liquid-glass-operational
entries.summary: LIQUID GLASS OPERATIONAL — large rounded translucent glass capsules drifting and overlapping, with soft white rim highlights, a faint inner sheen and thin refraction lines bending through each body. Calm, premium, operational.

entries.name: magnetic-vector
entries.summary: Canvas scene "magnetic-vector".

entries.name: motion-curve-field
entries.summary: Canvas scene "motion-curve-field".

entries.name: musebase-coordination
entries.summary: MUSEBASE COORDINATION — a central core with four module clusters (scheduling, communication, records, payment) orbiting on a wide ring;

entries.name: node-compression
entries.summary: NODE COMPRESSION — scattered nodes breathe inward to a centred ordered ring lattice then disperse; connector lines thicken and brighten at peak compression, red core.

entries.name: orbital-command
entries.summary: ORBITAL COMMAND — a single command ring of evenly spaced route nodes with short packets routing along inter-node chords and a pulsing accent core.

entries.name: permission-orbit
entries.summary: PERMISSION ORBIT — role/permission nodes orbit a central lock core on three concentric rings, each rotating at its own rate; a thin radial connector to a node blinks red as the node sweeps past the vertical "grant" axis.

entries.name: polar-status
entries.summary: POLAR STATUS — a single instrument dial: a radial tick gauge with a red arc that fills to a slowly drifting setpoint, satellite readout dots on an outer ring, and a thin sweeping indicator needle. Pointer nudges the setpoint.

entries.name: privacy-quiet-grid
entries.summary: PRIVACY QUIET GRID — a calm legal-page grid: a slow faint line grid, an occasional soft scan band drifting through long pauses, and a few slow-drifting tick marks that tick faintly red at their dwell points.

entries.name: radar-cutaway
entries.summary: RADAR CUTAWAY — a quarter radar anchored to the bottom-left corner: range rings and bearing spokes clipped to a 90deg wedge, a sweeping arm that paints contacts red as it crosses them, with blips that bloom then fade behind the sweep.

entries.name: radial-audio-core
entries.summary: RADIAL AUDIO CORE — a centred radial spectrum. drawRadialBars fans out from a white core ring, driven by live audio.bands (idle procedural when silent). Loud beats spawn outward-expanding pulse rings;

entries.name: redacted-timeline-branch
entries.summary: REDACTED TIMELINE BRANCH — a horizontal timeline spine with ticking time markers;

entries.name: research-blackout
entries.summary: RESEARCH BLACKOUT — rows of redacted/blacked-out bars over a dark field; a slow horizontal scan band sweeps across, momentarily exposing bars it passes, while rare cells flicker a partial red reveal. Mostly dark and ominous.

entries.name: scheduling-grid
entries.summary: SCHEDULING GRID — an abstract week planner: vertical lanes split by horizontal time rows, booking blocks of varying length fade in and out across the lanes, and a vertical "now" line sweeps left->right lighting blocks it crosses;

entries.name: secure-boundary
entries.summary: SECURE BOUNDARY — a central protected zone ringed by a slowly rotating dashed perimeter with a single accent gate aperture; access nodes drift in from outside and either thread the gate into the core or deflect off the wall.

entries.name: signal-spectrum-field
entries.summary: Canvas scene "signal-spectrum-field".

entries.name: split-prism
entries.summary: SPLIT PRISM — the field sliced by several parallel diagonal seams whose offsets drift; each pane carries a faint distinct texture (fine lines / dot lattice / blank), and a bright edge highlight runs along the seams.

entries.name: status-pulse-grid
entries.summary: STATUS PULSE GRID — a system monitor matrix of square status tiles; diagonal activation waves sweep across, lighting tiles as they pass; most tiles sit dim, a sparse few latch to a red "alert" state. Pointer drags a local hot zone.

entries.name: tooling-console
entries.summary: TOOLING CONSOLE — a faint terminal: a prompt with a blinking caret, left-aligned mono glyph lines that type in char-by-char, and a command-palette box that slides in from the right then retracts, its top entry highlighted red.

entries.name: topology-pulse
entries.summary: TOPOLOGY PULSE — horizontal topographic contour lines crossed by a bright radial pulse ring that expands from a slowly drifting emitter, lifting nearby contours.

entries.name: transaction-wave
entries.summary: TRANSACTION WAVE — a commerce throughput ticker: transaction spikes erupt upward from a baseline at varying heights, a slow cumulative line climbs across, faint value gridlines behind. Markets/throughput shape language, no full grid.

entries.name: trigger-action-pulse
entries.summary: TRIGGER ACTION PULSE — trigger nodes on the left fire pulses along rule-lines (some branching) to action nodes on the right, which flash red on arrival; a cause-and-effect automation rhythm.

entries.name: unknown-silhouette
entries.summary: UNKNOWN SILHOUETTE — a large blacked-out irregular polygon mass sits centre, breathing slowly with a faint rim and rare red edge leaks; a sparse corner-bracket scanning frame and a column of redacted readout ticks surround it.

entries.name: workflow-river
entries.summary: WORKFLOW RIVER — many near-parallel curved streamlines drifting left-to-right like a braided river, with directional flow particles riding the exact curves at varying per-lane speed; sparse red marks the leading current.

entries.name: redaction-matrix
entries.summary: A field of black metadata bars with a scan line that briefly "decrypts" the bars it passes over — classified / redacted mood.

entries.name: signal-wave
entries.summary: Oscilloscope signal — a centered horizontal waveform of summed sines that scrolls continuously over a faint grid, flanked by two fainter secondary waves, with a red leading dot tracing the main trace.

entries.name: spline-ribbon
entries.summary: Flowing bezier ribbons drifting across the field — a data stream.

entries.name: timeline-pulse
entries.summary: A horizontal baseline through evenly spaced nodes. A bright red pulse sweeps left-to-right repeatedly, igniting each node as it passes. Faint vertical ticks drop beneath every node; the line itself is faint white.

entries.name: topographic-lines
entries.summary: Flowing contour / topology lines that breathe like terrain.

entries.name: vector-compass
entries.summary: Vector direction field: a fixed grid of short arrow segments whose angles track flowAngle(x,y,t) and rotate smoothly, like compasses leaning into an invisible current. Faint white, sparse red. Cells are static;

entries.name: voronoi-cell
entries.summary: Computational cell field — jittered sites drift and connect to their 2–3 nearest neighbours, approximating Voronoi cell walls without the cost of a full diagram. A few accent sites pulse red.

entries.name: wave-interference
entries.summary: Layered sine-wave interference field — calm, signal-like horizontal bands.
